answer: Proposal: each knoll or karst survey ID/day delivers an assigned map and burns 5 credits. The registry checks finalized burns of that amount and trusted client-signed map receipts, both ID/day-bound; failure denies listing. Burns are recurring expense; machines are reusable capital; no locked stake. Client collusion can fake delivery; cheap credits weaken deterrence. Assuming irreversible burns, each burn counts once: shared hardware or a parallel thread cannot reduce ten IDs' burn below 50 credits/day. This meters paid entries, not owners.
